question: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹12,000 and sells it for ₹13,500. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price = ₹13,500 − ₹12,000 = ₹1,500

Profit % = (₹1,500 ÷ ₹12,000) × 100

Profit % = 12.5%

**∴ Answer = 12.5%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹12,000

Selling Price (SP) = ₹13,500

**Formula used:**

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
 
 
• 
 CP = ₹12,000
 SP = ₹13,500
 Profit = ₹1,500

**Calculations:**

Profit = SP − CP = ₹13,500 − ₹12,000 = ₹1,500

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (₹1,500 ÷ ₹12,000) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% (Option 3).**
